provider_policy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which language tag identifies this linguistic context, and in which canonical form is it stored?
Which subtags does the tag contain and what role does each one play?
Is the tag well-formed only, or also valid against the subtag registry?
Which casing and subtag ordering conventions were applied, and are they treated as significant for comparison?
Does the tag carry private-use or otherwise unregistered subtags, and what do they mean inside the adopting Dimension?
Which registry snapshot, identified by its File-Date, was used to validate these subtags?
Is any subtag or the whole tag deprecated, and what replacement does the registry record prescribe?
Is the identifier a grandfathered or redundant registration, and how is it mapped forward?
Does the primary language subtag denote a macrolanguage, a collection or an extended language, and which encompassed language is actually meant?
How is drift between a stored identifier and a newer registry snapshot detected and reconciled?
Which ISO 15924 script code applies to this linguistic context?
Was the script subtag omitted because the registry records a Suppress-Script value for that language?
If the script was not declared, how was it inferred and with what confidence?
Does the content mix writing systems, and how is that recorded without altering the declared tag?
What base direction is declared for this string or resource, and at which scope?
Was the direction stated explicitly or produced by a first-strong heuristic, and what residual risk remains?
Which character order and line order apply to the layout of this content?
How are language and direction metadata preserved when a value is embedded in another string or transferred between systems?
Which Unicode locale identifier applies here, and how does it differ from the plain language identifier recorded for the same context?
Which Unicode extension keys and types are asserted, and which values are merely environment defaults?
Does a transformed-content extension declare that this value was derived from another language, and from which source?
Which canonicalization was applied to the extension sequence, and were duplicate attributes or keys dropped?
How does the consuming boundary handle extension keys it does not recognise or support?
Which convention profiles does this locale declaration select, and where are their definitions maintained?
Which data release supplied each referenced profile, and is that release pinned or floating?
Where does responsibility for the actual formatting, parsing or sorting behaviour sit?
What is recorded when a selected convention profile is unavailable in the consuming environment?
Which ordered language ranges express the requested preference, and in what priority order?
Are the supplied ranges basic or extended, and do any of them contain wildcards?
Are relative weights attached to the ranges, and how are ties and zero weights treated?
Where did this preference come from, and is it a stated choice or an inferred signal?
What limits apply to reusing this preference outside the interaction that produced it?
Which locales are available within this scope, and at what granularity is availability asserted?
How complete is each available locale, and what threshold counts as available at all?
Which locale is the configured default when no requested range matches anything available?
How often is the inventory regenerated, and how are stale entries detected?
Which matching scheme was applied, with which parameters, and is it deterministic across hosts?
Which locale was resolved, and is it an exact match, a truncation or the configured default?
What fallback chain was traversed, and what reason is recorded for each step?
When was the resolution performed, and against which inventory version and registry snapshot?
Who may override or re-run a resolution, and where is the override recorded?
What role does this declaration play: the language of the content, the intended audience, or the interface locale?
Which party or system asserted this declaration, and on what authority?
Was the language declared by an authority or automatically detected, and how is a disagreement between the two settled?
Which declaration prevails when several apply at different scopes to the same content?
Which identifier designates this translatable unit independently of its source text, and within which scope is that identifier unique?
Which source-text revision is currently in force for this unit, and how is that revision denoted and verified?
What context, meaning, purpose or audience notes disambiguate this unit for a translator or an agent?
What must happen to existing bindings when the source text changes while the unit identifier stays the same?
Which content node, message or media element in the owning system does this unit correspond to?
Is this unit or span marked as translatable, and which rule or inheritance established that value?
Which literal tokens, codes or brand strings must appear unchanged in every target variant?
To which locales does this unit apply, and is that list inclusive or exclusive?
How is a breach of a protected token, allowed-character set or storage-size limit detected before publication?
Which canonicalised language tag and variant revision together identify this target variant of the unit?
What translation state does this variant hold, and who is authorised to advance it to the next state?
Is this variant stale relative to the current source revision, and by which comparison was that decided?
When was this variant produced, reviewed or approved, and when was each of those facts recorded here?
Was the target text produced by a machine, by a human, or by a mixed post-editing process?
Which external resource holds the actual target content, and how is it addressed and dereferenced?
What digest or version pin makes the referenced resource verifiable at a stated point in time?
Which non-text or time-based media alternatives must accompany this variant in this locale?
What is asserted when the referenced resource is unreachable or its digest no longer matches?
Which selectors does this message declare, and in what order are they evaluated against variant keys?
Which plural or select categories must the target variant supply for its own language?
Is a catch-all variant present so that every possible selector value resolves to a pattern?
Are the categories cardinal plural, ordinal, or an enumerated select set defined by the message author?
Which named variables and placeholders must appear in the target, and may they be copied, deleted or reordered?
What value type, function or option constraints apply to each placeholder?
How are original formatting codes and markup kept isolated from the translatable text of this unit?
How is bidirectional isolation applied around placeholders in mixed-direction text?
What is emitted when a placeholder or variable cannot be resolved at format time?
What is the ordered list of language tags or locales tried when the requested variant is absent?
What is the terminal behaviour when no entry in the chain matches?
Which chain position actually supplied the value served, and was that entry inherited or an override?
Is the consumer told that the served text is a fallback rather than a translation into the requested language?
Under what conditions is fallback prohibited and an explicit absence or error preferred instead?
Which terminology concept does this term occurrence denote, and in which termbase does that concept live?
Which target term is preferred, admitted or deprecated for that concept in this target locale?
How is a term-usage breach recorded when the approved target term is not used?
What evidence supports a term identification made automatically rather than by a terminologist?
What confidence value does the producing system assert for this variant, and on which declared scale?
Which quality issues were recorded against this variant, of what type and at what severity?
Against which published quality profile and score threshold was any overall rating computed?
What proportion of the unit set has an approved variant in this locale, and how is that proportion defined?
Which entries does the coverage measure exclude, and is fallback-served content excluded from it?
Which person, organisation or tool produced the target text, and which agent revised it?
What review was performed on this variant, and under whose authority was it signed off?
Where is the full workflow task history held, and what exactly is referenced from here?
What personal data appears in translator and reviewer attribution, and how is it minimised?
How long must a review assertion be retained after the variant it describes is superseded?
Which pseudo-locale runs were executed against this unit set, and what defects did they expose?
Did the rendered target text fit the declared size, storage and layout constraints?
Which build or product revision was verified, and when was the run observed?
Which defect classes remain untested by pseudo-localization and rendering checks alone?
Which named party is accountable for this localization binding on the host object?
Which roles are authorized to propose, vet, review, approve and release a change to this binding?
How is contributor standing weighted when locale expertise is distributed across several organizations?
What is recorded when no qualified language expert or release authority is available for a target locale?
Who is authorized to declare the default locale and the ordered fallback chain for this host object?
Which matching scheme governs resolution, and what behaviour is defined when no tag matches?
Which regional or organizational locale profile constrains the tags permitted on this binding?
Which subtag combinations does that profile require, prohibit or normalize away?
Which agent generated or revised each bound language tag, translation or term, and in what role?
What evidence supports an inferred or machine-generated value, and what confidence accompanies it?
Which prior binding version or upstream source is this value derived from or a revision of?
At what confidence threshold must an inferred locale or translation be escalated to human review?
Which language subtag registry revision was in force when this binding was validated?
Which locale-data release and profile revision were pinned for fallback and likely-subtag resolution?
Which exchange-format and terminology standard versions does this binding claim alignment with?
What triggers re-validation when a pinned registry, profile or standard revision advances?
Is the bound tag well-formed, valid against the pinned registry, and in canonical form?
Does the binding satisfy the declared profile's permitted-tag and required-subtag constraints?
How is a deprecated subtag with a preferred value mapped without silently rewriting the recorded original?
How is the declared tag reconciled against detected or transport-asserted content language?
Which precedence rule applies when the declared tag, the transport-level claim and the profile default disagree?
How is a conflict between a macrolanguage tag and a more specific individual-language tag recorded?
What is recorded when a cultural or accessibility review cannot be completed for a target locale?
Which accessibility obligations does this binding discharge, and which remain with the rendering layer?
Which external carrier fields does this binding map onto for interchange?
Is each mapping lossless, lossy or one-way, and what is dropped on round-trip?
Which identifier correlates the binding with an external localization unit across systems?
What evidence supports each claimed alignment, and is conformance asserted or only alignment?
What is the current workflow state of this binding and which transitions are permitted from it?
Over which effective interval is this binding version authoritative for the host object?
Which binding version supersedes or is superseded by this one, and on what ground?
How is an erroneous published binding corrected without destroying the superseded record?
When is a binding deprecated with replacement guidance rather than withdrawn outright?
Which localized findings or artifacts are restricted, and to which audience classes?
Until what moment is a localized variant embargoed, and what may be disclosed before it?
Does the localized value contain personal or otherwise regulated data that constrains disclosure?
What redaction or substitution is applied when an unauthorized audience requests the binding?
What retention class and minimum retention period apply to this binding record?
Is the binding subject to a hold that blocks disposition, and who asserted it?
What integrity evidence shows that a superseded binding version is unaltered?
What must a tombstone preserve after a binding is withdrawn, and who executes the destruction?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
